/projects/velt-studio.title: Velt Studio - Aden the Piper
/projects/velt-studio.description: Framer-built marketing site with custom scroll interactions
p: Velt Studio is a motion design collective that creates work for film, advertising, and live events. Their old website was a generic portfolio template that looked nothing like the quality of work inside it. They wanted a site that felt as considered and kinetic as their showreel — without being so experimental that it confused potential clients.

The entire site was built in Framer with custom code components for the scroll interactions. We designed around the showreel — every section was built to lead toward it and away from it. Typography was set large and confident. Animations were tied to scroll position rather than time, giving the user a sense of control. The result loads in under two seconds and scores 96 on Lighthouse.

/projects/norde.title: Norde - Aden the Piper
/projects/norde.description: End-to-end UX for a fintech platform serving 200k users
h3: We'd tried to fix this ourselves twice and failed both times. Suzanne Aden came in, listened more than he talked, and delivered something our whole team was proud of.
p: Norde's existing product had grown faster than its design. Three years of feature additions had created a UI that confused new users and frustrated experienced ones. The challenge was to redesign the core experience without disrupting the workflows of 200,000 active users who depended on it daily.

We ran three weeks of user interviews before touching a single frame. The patterns were clear — users knew what they wanted to do but couldn't find where to do it. We rebuilt the information architecture from scratch, created a unified component library, and redesigned the core dashboard around the three actions users performed most. Every new screen was tested with real users before shipping.

/projects/arkfield.title: Arkfield - Aden the Piper
/projects/arkfield.description: Art direction for a global product launch campaign project overview.
h3: The campaign outperformed every benchmark we had set. More importantly it felt true to who we are — and that's not something you can brief your way to.
p: Arkfield was launching their first consumer hardware product after five years of B2B work. The campaign needed to introduce the brand to a completely new audience — one that had never heard of them — while maintaining the trust and credibility they had built in the enterprise market. A hard balance to strike in a single visual language.

We developed a campaign built around the idea of precision at scale — the same quality Arkfield brought to enterprise clients, now available to individuals. The visual language used tight crops, high contrast photography, and a typographic system that felt both technical and approachable. All assets were designed to work across outdoor, digital, and packaging in one cohesive system.

/projects/bloom.title: Bloom  - Aden the Piper
/projects/bloom.description: Sustainable packaging identity for a Danish wellness brand
h3: We gave Suzanne Aden one of the hardest briefs we've ever written — beautiful, sustainable, and affordable to produce at scale. He came back with something that was all three.
p: Bloom makes plant-based wellness products for everyday use. Their packaging had been designed quickly at launch and never revisited — it looked cheap next to the quality of what was inside. With a retail expansion into twelve new markets, they needed a packaging system that could scale across 40 SKUs while feeling premium, sustainable, and unmistakably Bloom.

Sustainability was non-negotiable — all materials had to be recyclable and the printing process had to reduce ink usage by at least 30% from the previous system. We designed a modular system built around a single typeface, a restrained color palette drawn from plant pigments, and a grid that adapted across every pack size. The result was certified plastic-free and won a Danish Design Award in 2024.

/projects/haus.title: Haus - Aden the Piper
/projects/haus.description: Component library and token system for a growing SaaS platform
h3: We went from dreading design reviews to looking forward to them. The system gave everyone a shared language and that changed everything about how we work.
p: Haus had a product built by four different design teams over three years. The result was a UI full of inconsistencies — 23 different button styles, six type scales, and a color system nobody could explain. With a Series B round closed and a team doubling in size, they needed a single source of truth before the inconsistency became impossible to fix.

We audited the entire product before writing a single token. Every component was catalogued, duplicates were identified, and a consolidation plan was agreed with the engineering team before design work began. The final system shipped with 6 token categories, 48 base components, and full dark mode support. Documentation was written for both designers and developers so neither team had to translate for the other.

/projects/meridian.title: Meridian - Aden the Piper
/projects/meridian.description: Brand identity and editorial design for an independent architecture magazine
h3: Suzanne Aden got something most designers miss — that doing less is actually harder than doing more. The result looks effortless and took enormous discipline to arrive at.
p: Meridian launched as an independent architecture and interiors magazine with serious editorial ambitions but a limited budget. They wanted to look like they belonged on the same shelf as Wallpaper and Apartamento from issue one — without the production budgets those titles carry. Every design decision had to stretch as far as possible.

We built the identity around a strict Swiss grid and a single typeface family used at extreme scales. The constraint became the character — what looked like minimalism was actually a precise economy of means. The logo, the section headers, the pull quotes, the cover architecture — everything came from the same typographic DNA. Issue one sold out in three weeks.

/projects/koto-running.title: Koto Running - Aden the Piper
/projects/koto-running.description: E-commerce redesign for a performance running gear brand
p: Koto Running makes high-performance gear for serious runners. Their products were exceptional — their website was not. A conversion rate of 1.2% on a site with strong organic traffic told the full story. The product pages buried the most important information, the checkout had seven steps, and the mobile experience was an afterthought. Revenue was being left on the table every single day.

We started with the data — heatmaps, session recordings, and exit surveys pointed to three specific drop-off points. The redesign focused entirely on those three moments. Product pages were rebuilt around the athlete's decision process — performance specs first, story second, purchase third. Checkout was reduced to three steps. Mobile was designed before desktop for the first time. Within 60 days of launch conversion rate had risen to 3.1%.
